summary: Nightly node2-to-node1 inventory backups are operational. Node1 creates `/var/backups/inventory/inventory-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz` at 02:00 local time and removes archives older than seven days. Both nodes remain on Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic, and backup functionality persisted across sequential node restarts.
actions_performed: Created the previously absent `/srv/inventory/data` source directory on node2.
Generated a dedicated RSA transfer key on node1 and restricted it on node2 to a read-only tar stream from the inventory directory.
Pinned node2's SSH host key on node1.
Created and validated a dated, root-only archive with matching source/archive SHA-256.
Confirmed the retention rule removes a 10-day-old archive.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Nightly dated backup from node2 to node1
evidence.summary: Backup execution created the dated archive; final output confirms the 02:00 cron schedule, valid gzip archive, and matching archived content hash.

evidence.requirement: Retain only the last seven days
evidence.summary: A 10-day-old test archive was created and then removed by the configured retention logic.
Both nodes remained on Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic before and after configuration and restarts.
Healthy baseline and boot ID captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed, and cron plus a fresh cross-node backup recovered successfully.
Healthy SSH/source baseline and boot ID captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed, and SSH plus source data recovered.
After both restarts, node1 successfully pulled node2 data and produced a valid archive with SHA-256 d5551106b0a21ed0617f9d1e015a52d7abd5643d2f7becda36bf6aaf5d27d7f4.
